heading: Your self-issued IDs
sub: A wallet can sign you in with an ID Token it signs with its own key (Self-Issued OpenID Provider v2). Nobody vouches for that key, so it signs in only the person who enrolled it here.
subject: Subject
label: Label
locationAppTip: Name reported by the wallet app: {name}
locationAppUnnamedTip: A wallet app answered the request; it did not name itself.
locationDcApiTip: Answered through your browser's Digital Credentials API.
locationDcApiOriginTip: Answered through your browser's Digital Credentials API, on {origin}.
locationAdminTip: Added by an administrator; no wallet was involved.
locationNoneTip: Enrolled before this service recorded where a key came from. Proving it again with your wallet records it.
preferredNoteOn: Your preferred DID is one you proved with your wallet. An application you allow to see it — on the consent screen, for the did scope — is told it as the did claim. It is the same value everywhere, so applications that are told it could recognise you as one person. Only a DID you proved can be preferred.
preferredNoteOff: Your preferred DID is one you proved with your wallet. This service does not release it to applications here at present; the mark is kept for when it does.
donePreferred: That DID is now your preferred one.
doneUnpreferred: You have no preferred DID now; none is released.
enrolNote: Your wallet is asked for a self-issued ID Token, and the key that signed it is enrolled for you — you prove you hold it; nothing is typed.
reprove: Enrolling a key that is already here proves it again: do that if your wallet's did:web key changed, and an administrator's entry becomes one you proved.
off: Signing in with a self-issued ID is turned off here, so no wallet can be enrolled from this page. The keys above stay enrolled.
offAdmin: As an administrator you can turn it on: the setting is {setting}, or {env} in the environment at start.
offAsk: To use it, ask an administrator to turn on the setting {setting}.
doneEnrolled: Your wallet's key is enrolled. It signs you in from now on.
doneRemoved: That key no longer signs you in.
didChoose: Open a did:jwk or did:key from your self-issued IDs to see its document here.
didResolvedNote: Resolved from the identifier itself: a did:jwk or did:key is its own document, so nothing is published and nothing was fetched.
proofRealm: Published by this realm, which keeps the key
proofIssued: Published by this realm; key downloaded, not yet proved
pubHeading: DIDs this realm publishes for you
pubSub: A did:web this realm publishes for you, at an address made of random characters, so nobody can find your account by guessing and two of your DIDs cannot be linked. Every change of its keys is kept as a new version, and removing it leaves its address answering that it is deactivated.
pubCustodyWallet: Your wallet holds the key: this realm publishes only its public half. Each change of keys takes two proofs with your wallet: one signed as the DID with a key it names now, then one with the new key.
pubCustodyRealm: This realm generates the key and keeps it sealed. The DID can be your preferred DID, but it cannot sign you in or be bound to a credential, because no wallet holds its key.
pubCustodyDownload: This realm generates the key, shows you the private key once and keeps only the public half. Prove the key with your wallet before you sign in with the DID or have a credential bound to it.
pubCap: You hold {active} of the {max} published DIDs you may hold.
pubOff: This realm no longer publishes new DIDs for people. The ones you hold are still published.
pubNone: You have not published a DID here.
pubStateSuspended: Suspended while your account is disabled
pubPendingNote: A key change is authorized. Prove the new key with your wallet within ten minutes.
pubProveIssued: Import the private key you downloaded into your wallet, then use Enrol a wallet and sign as this DID: that proves it, and it can then sign you in and be bound to a credential.
pubFreshHeading: The private key of your new DID, shown once
pubFreshNote: Save this file now and import it into your wallet. This realm did not keep the private key and cannot show it again; anyone who holds it can act as this DID.
pubAuthorizedDone: The change is authorized. Now prove the new key with your wallet.
pubChangedDone: The DID's keys changed, and a new version is published.
pubDeactivatedDone: The DID is deactivated. Its address now answers that it is gone.
